memory_update.text: Hammond Power Solutions should be tracked as the most direct underfollowed dry-type transformer and power-quality candidate for this node, but primary listing is TSX and U.S. access appears OTC; later layers must verify investability, liquidity, and current market cap.

Powell Industries is a high-conviction direct U.S.-listed switchgear/power-distribution candidate, supported by official FY2026 backlog and data-center order evidence, but attention and valuation risk may have increased after the $400M-plus order disclosure.

nVent is a larger reference/adjacent platform for data-center electrical connection, protection, enclosures, power distribution, and switchgear/bus systems; include mainly as a comp and customer-demand read-through rather than a pure transformer bottleneck name.

Pioneer Power Solutions requires deeper verification before promotion beyond speculative_shadow: confirm current segment perimeter after business changes, whether transformer/switchgear exposure is still material, and whether backlog/profitability support the chokepoint thesis.

Hammond Power Solutions is the strongest direct fit for the dry-type transformers, power-quality, and magnetics node, but US accessibility/liquidity requires verification because the primary evidence references HPS.A rather than a main US listing.

Preformed Line Products is not a dry-type transformer supplier but should remain in the adjacent grid-hardware discovery lane as a potential second-order beneficiary of transmission and interconnection buildouts.

The node appears to overlap three investable buckets: direct transformer and power-quality suppliers, broader electrical-distribution equipment leaders, and adjacent transmission/distribution hardware suppliers that benefit from the same grid-capex cycle.

Need a follow-up search specifically for US-listed small/mid-cap dry-type transformer, switchgear, magnetics, capacitor, power-conditioning, and custom-electrical-equipment manufacturers beyond HPS, PLPC, HUBB, and ETN.

POWL is the cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidate for switchgear/electrical distribution exposure, but its market cap has moved above the preferred USD 300M-10B range; keep only if later evidence confirms data-center/commercial utility demand is material.
AMSC maps to the power-quality and voltage-stability sub-node rather than dry-type transformer manufacturing; retain as second-order grid-stability candidate pending order/backlog verification.

PLPC is not in the transformer/switchgear core node but may be an obscure second-order supplier to transmission/distribution buildout; later layers should test whether it benefits before EPC revenue recognition.

PPSI has direct switchgear/e-Bloc language but is a below-USD-300M micro-cap exception; survival requires unusually strong evidence on backlog conversion, margins, cash runway, customer quality, and dilution risk.

Hammond Power Solutions appears to be one of the most relevant North American dry-type transformer/power-quality pure plays, but primary listing is Canadian. Consider a separate non-US-listed comp lane or OTC/liquidity check if the dashboard permits non-US primary listings.

For US-listed names, pure dry-type transformer exposure is scarce; the practical investable map shifts toward switchgear, engineered power distribution, voltage-control/power-quality systems, and transmission/distribution hardware.

HMDPF/Hammond Power Solutions is the cleanest underfollowed direct candidate for dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and magnetics, but U.S. tradability and primary TSX disclosure need verification.

POWL/Powell Industries is a strong adjacent switchgear and packaged power-distribution candidate; market cap now appears above the ideal $300M-$10B range, so treat it as a reference-underfollowed hybrid rather than a hidden small-cap.
BELFB/Bel Fuse maps the theme one layer down into power conversion, protection, and magnetic components for data-center, networking, industrial, and electrification applications.

PPSI/Pioneer Power Solutions is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate only; it requires unusually strict falsification around current revenue mix, liquidity, dilution, backlog, and whether transformer/switchgear exposure remains material.

Need next-pass verification from primary filings for Hammond, Powell, Bel Fuse, and Pioneer: backlog, end-market mix, data-center exposure, lead times, capacity expansion, customer concentration, and margin sustainability.
